newsitem.title: GERMANY: Cold War spy exchange bridge to be replaced.
newsitem.headline: Cold War spy exchange bridge to be replaced.

text.p: The Glienicke bridge used for Cold War spy exchanges will have to be replaced within the next decade because the steel in the 90-year-old structure is weakening, German officials said on Thursday.
The green steel bridge built in 1906 spanning the Havel River was closed after the Berlin Wall was built in 1961, cutting off a main connecting route between West Berlin and Potsdam.
The bridge became famous for its Cold War exchanges of spies such as American U2 pilot Gary Powers. Soviet Jewish dissident Anatoly Shcharansky was also exchanged there.
Hartmut Wienhoefer, spokesman for the Water and Shipping authority in Berlin, said the bridge's steel would become brittle by the year 2006 -- its 100th anniversary -- and would have to be replaced.
"It is a question of safety," Wienhoefer said.
The exact fate of the bridge is still unclear. Because it is protected by the United Nations as a cultural landmark, authorities will have to design a plan with local monument preservation agencies.
